title: WAR ROOM CRISIS
description: Navigate high-stakes emergency meetings, manage Chaos Levels, and practice incident response English under pressure.

levels.name: CRISIS 1: SERVER DOWN!
levels.description: A production API outage caused an 85% error rate surge during peak hours.

scenarios.speaker: CTO (Chief Technology Officer)
scenarios.prompt: The API error rate surged to 85%. The CTO joins the emergency War Room and asks: "Team, what is our current situation?"

options.text: We've detected an 85% drop in API availability. The team is currently isolating the root cause between the database cluster and the latest build.
options.feedback: Flawless status report! Concise, factual, and action-oriented.

options.text: I think something broke after the last commit, but we are looking into it.
options.feedback: Vague statement. In crisis meetings, state clear metrics and active investigation steps.

options.text: Everything is broken! I told everyone not to deploy on Friday!
options.feedback: Panic & blame! This spikes the Chaos Level significantly.

scenarios.explanation: In emergency meetings, leaders require factual, calm status reports that state scope and action without assigning blame.

scenarios.speaker: Database Engineer Lead
scenarios.prompt: High lock contention is reported on the database cluster. How do you coordinate next steps with Infrastructure?

options.text: Could Infrastructure check the active connection pool while Backend reviews recent slow queries?
options.feedback: Excellent parallel task delegation using polite imperatives!

options.text: Database team, just fix the locks so we can go back to work.
options.feedback: Dismissive tone. A collaborative approach gets better results.

options.text: Let's restart all production servers right now and see what happens!
options.feedback: Reckless proposal! Restarting without diagnosis can worsen outage time.

scenarios.explanation: Effective technical coordination uses parallel delegation ('Could [Team A] do X while [Team B] does Y?').

scenarios.speaker: Head of Sales (Interrupter)
scenarios.prompt: The Head of Sales interrupts: "Acme Corp is losing $10k per minute! Why isn't this fixed yet?!"

options.text: I understand the urgency. We are currently testing a fix and will provide a status update in 10 minutes.
options.feedback: Masterful diplomatic response! Acknowledges urgency and sets a clear timeframe.

options.text: Please stop interrupting us, we are trying to code!
options.feedback: Aggressive posture increases meeting friction.

options.text: It's not my fault! Talk to the DevOps team!
options.feedback: Shifting blame under pressure damages trust across teams.

scenarios.explanation: De-escalate panicked interruptions by acknowledging business impact and committing to timed status updates.

scenarios.speaker: DevOps Lead
scenarios.prompt: DevOps wants to rollback to release v2.4, but Frontend wants to push a hotfix. You must pitch the safest strategy.

options.text: To minimize downtime, I recommend rolling back to v2.4 immediately while we test the hotfix in staging.
options.feedback: Strategic decision! Prioritizes system stability and risk mitigation.

options.text: Maybe we can try the hotfix, but if it fails we can rollback later?
options.feedback: Hesitant proposal. In critical incidents, clear recommendations inspire confidence.

options.text: Let's deploy both at the same time and hope one works!
options.feedback: Extreme risk! Dual deployments introduce unmanageable variables.

scenarios.explanation: Pitching incident solutions requires highlighting risk minimization ('To minimize downtime, I recommend...').

scenarios.speaker: Meeting Facilitator
scenarios.prompt: The rollback succeeded and traffic is stabilizing. You must assign action items before concluding.

options.text: Alex, will you take ownership of patching the memory leak? Maria, could you monitor metrics during the rollout?
options.feedback: Clear ownership and explicit task delegation!

options.text: Someone needs to fix the memory leak and someone else needs to watch metrics.
options.feedback: Unassigned tasks lead to bystander apathy. Name individuals directly.

options.text: I guess whoever has free time can check the memory leak later today.
options.feedback: Lack of accountability after a critical incident invites future outages.

scenarios.explanation: Action items must have clear ownership ('[Name], will you take ownership of [Task]?').

scenarios.speaker: CTO
scenarios.prompt: All metrics are green (100% normal). How do you conclude the War Room meeting professionally?

options.text: Great teamwork everyone. I'll publish the incident post-mortem in Slack by 3 PM and schedule a root-cause review for tomorrow.
options.feedback: Professional closure! Praises team effort and sets post-mortem deliverables.

options.text: Okay, it seems fixed now. Let's just forget about this.
options.feedback: Ignoring post-mortems prevents team learning and continuous improvement.

options.text: Thank goodness that's over. I never want to see this code again!
options.feedback: Unprofessional conclusion.

scenarios.explanation: Conclude incident meetings by confirming post-mortem reports and root cause analysis schedules.

levels.name: CRISIS 2: SECURITY BREACH!
levels.description: Unauthorized access was detected on production API keys. Security breach protocol activated.

scenarios.speaker: CISO (Chief Information Security Officer)
scenarios.prompt: An automated alert detected leaked admin API keys on GitHub. CISO asks: "Has customer data been compromised?"

options.text: We are actively auditing audit logs to determine exposure. I recommend revoking the compromised key immediately.
options.feedback: Clear containment strategy! Focuses on immediate mitigation and log auditing.

options.text: We aren't sure yet, maybe nobody noticed the key on GitHub.
options.feedback: Dangerous wishful thinking! Assume leaked keys are compromised instantly.

options.text: Who leaked the key?! We need to fire whoever did this right now!
options.feedback: Panic & witch-hunting! Resolving the security threat comes before investigation.

scenarios.explanation: During security incidents, focus immediately on key revocation and containment before assigning fault.

scenarios.speaker: Lead Security Engineer
scenarios.prompt: Security wants to force global token revocation, but Product Manager worries it will disconnect 50,000 active users.

options.text: To secure customer data, we must revoke active tokens now and send an automated re-authentication notification to users.
options.feedback: Decisive security leadership! Prioritizes data security with clear user communication.

options.text: Let's wait until tonight so we don't annoy our active users.
options.feedback: Delaying token revocation during an active breach exposes user data to theft.

options.text: Let Product Manager decide, it's not a technical choice.
options.feedback: Abdicating security responsibility increases breach liability.

scenarios.explanation: Security breaches require decisive action ('We must revoke active tokens now and send...').

scenarios.speaker: Head of Public Relations (Interrupter)
scenarios.prompt: PR Manager interrupts: "TechCrunch is tweeting about a leak! What statement can I release to the press?"

options.text: Please inform PR that we are preparing an official incident statement with Legal and will share it within 30 minutes.
options.feedback: Masterful media containment! Prevents uncoordinated press statements.

options.text: Just tell them it was a small glitch and everything is fine!
options.feedback: Downplaying breaches without legal review leads to severe regulatory fines.

options.text: No comment! Tell them to go away!
options.feedback: Hostile PR responses damage company reputation severely.

scenarios.explanation: Coordinate security statements through official channels ('...share an official incident statement with Legal').

scenarios.speaker: DevOps Architect
scenarios.prompt: DevOps proposes implementing Vault secrets management immediately. How do you pitch this to the team?

options.text: To prevent future credential leaks, I propose migrating all secret keys to HashiCorp Vault during tonight's maintenance window.
options.feedback: Proactive security proposal with clear scheduling!

options.text: We should probably use Vault, but it sounds like a lot of work.
options.feedback: Lack of conviction weakens architectural proposals.

options.text: Let's just tell developers to stop uploading keys to GitHub.
options.feedback: Relying on memory instead of automated secret scanning fails.

scenarios.explanation: Pitch security enhancements with rationale and timeframe ('To prevent X, I propose migrating Y during Z').

scenarios.speaker: Security Compliance Lead
scenarios.prompt: A forensic security audit must be conducted across all microservices. How do you assign responsibilities?

options.text: Carlos, please lead the audit on Payment Services. Sarah, could you scan the Auth service logs for suspicious IP addresses?
options.feedback: Direct assignment of forensic audit tasks!

options.text: Everyone check their own microservices when they have a chance.
options.feedback: Vague assignments mean critical microservices get overlooked.

options.text: I'll do the entire audit myself overnight.
options.feedback: Hero mentality creates bottlenecks and burnout during incidents.

scenarios.explanation: Delegate specialized tasks to specific engineers ('[Name], please lead the audit on [Component]').

scenarios.speaker: CISO
scenarios.prompt: Threat is neutralized and keys rotated. How do you report the final breach debrief to the executive board?

options.text: The threat has been fully contained, all keys rotated, and zero unauthorized data access was confirmed. A full compliance report will be delivered by 5 PM.
options.feedback: Executive-level summary! Clear containment, zero impact confirmation, and deliverable deadline.

options.text: We survived the breach! Let's hope it doesn't happen again.
options.feedback: Casual closure undermines executive confidence.

options.text: I'm still nervous about our servers, but I guess we can close the War Room.
options.feedback: Uncertainty at executive wrap-up prolongs crisis anxiety.

scenarios.explanation: Conclude security debriefs with definitive status ('The threat has been fully contained...').

levels.name: CRISIS 3: GLOBAL CLOUD MELTDOWN!
levels.description: Primary AWS region US-EAST-1 went completely dark. Global failover required under extreme time pressure.

scenarios.speaker: VP of Engineering
scenarios.prompt: AWS US-EAST-1 is completely unreachable. VP asks: "Can we initiate disaster recovery failover to EU-WEST immediately?"

options.text: Yes, our Disaster Recovery playbook is ready. I recommend switching DNS routing to EU-WEST right now.
options.feedback: Fast, confident execution of Disaster Recovery plans!

options.text: EU-WEST might be missing some recent user data, I'm scared to failover.
options.feedback: Hesitation during major cloud outages prolongs global downtime.

options.text: AWS promised 99.99% uptime! Let's wait for AWS engineers to fix it!
options.feedback: Passive reliance on third-party cloud providers spikes panic.

scenarios.explanation: In cloud outages, execute Disaster Recovery procedures immediately ('I recommend switching DNS routing to [Region]').

scenarios.speaker: Data Lead
scenarios.prompt: Database replica in EU-WEST has a 45-second replication lag. How do you manage potential data drift?

options.text: We will promote the EU replica to primary and log the 45-second gap for automated reconciliation once US-EAST recovers.
options.feedback: Pragmatic data engineering decision under pressure!

options.text: Don't promote the replica until lag is zero, even if it takes hours!
options.feedback: Waiting for a dead region to sync replication lag is impossible.

options.text: Who cares about 45 seconds of data? Just wipe it!
options.feedback: Casual data destruction destroys customer trust.

scenarios.explanation: Handle replication lag by planning post-incident data reconciliation.

scenarios.speaker: CTO of Enterprise Client (Angry Interrupter)
scenarios.prompt: CTO of Enterprise Client calls directly: "Our global operations are stalled! Give me a precise ETA!"

options.text: We are currently redirecting traffic to our European data center. Failover will complete in under 8 minutes.
options.feedback: Clear ETA and active progress update calms VIP clients.

options.text: It's AWS's fault, call Amazon support!
options.feedback: Blaming cloud vendors to enterprise clients sounds unprofessional.

options.text: I can't give you an ETA, maybe an hour or two.
options.feedback: Vague ETAs provoke contract cancellations.

scenarios.explanation: Provide concrete ETAs based on active recovery steps ('Failover will complete in under X minutes').

scenarios.speaker: CFO (Chief Financial Officer)
scenarios.prompt: CFO joins asking why single-region setup failed. Pitch multi-cloud active-active redundancy for the future.

options.text: To guarantee 99.99% availability, I propose investing in an Active-Active multi-cloud architecture starting next quarter.
options.feedback: Strategic architectural proposal aligned with business ROI!

options.text: Single region is cheap, that's why it failed.
options.feedback: Passive complaint instead of a constructive proposal.

options.text: We need millions of dollars right now or servers will keep crashing!
options.feedback: Alarmist financial demands destroy credibility with executive leadership.

scenarios.explanation: Pitch high-availability architecture as business ROI ('To guarantee 99.99% availability, I propose investing in...').

scenarios.speaker: DevOps Lead
scenarios.prompt: DNS failover is complete. How do you delegate health verification across team leads?

options.text: Frontend team, verify edge CDN routing. Database team, monitor connection metrics on EU-WEST.
options.feedback: Structured cross-team verification directives!

options.text: Can someone check if the site loads on their phone?
options.feedback: Informal testing is insufficient for enterprise disaster recovery.

options.text: Let's assume everything works if nobody complains.
options.feedback: Assuming stability without verification leads to hidden outages.

scenarios.explanation: Direct specialized teams to verify domain-specific health metrics.

scenarios.speaker: VP of Engineering
scenarios.prompt: Global traffic is 100% restored via EU-WEST. Conclude the multi-cloud emergency War Room.

options.text: Global failover is complete and system status is 100% operational. Outstanding work under pressure, team!
options.feedback: Inspirational leadership and professional incident closure!

options.text: That was horrible. Let's go home.
options.feedback: Negative sentiment spoils team achievement.

options.text: We got lucky this time, next outage will be worse.
options.feedback: Defeatist remarks demoralize incident response teams.

scenarios.explanation: Conclude disaster recovery incidents with victory acknowledgment and operational confirmation.
